subject: chemistry
title: Bonding Adventure 2 · Calculations
welcome_lead: Time to write some formulas — balancing charges in ionic compounds and counting bonds in small molecules.
meta_desc: GCSE Chemistry Bonding formulas — ionic balancing for NaCl, MgO, MgCl2, simple covalent molecules and giant covalent structures.
final_note: You can balance ionic charges to write formulas, recall simple covalent molecules, and spot giant covalent structures.

concepts.def: Diagram showing electrons from each atom in a bond.
Mg2+: magnesium loses two outer electrons.
CH4: one carbon shares with four hydrogens.
NH3: one nitrogen shares with three hydrogens.
Giant covalent: each C bonded to 4 others.

walkthroughs.body_html:
In an ionic formula the positive and negative charges must cancel.

Na+ and Cl- gives NaCl. Mg2+ and O2- gives MgO. Mg2+ and Cl- needs two chlorides, so MgCl2. Na+ and O2- needs two sodiums, so Na2O.

Non-metals share electrons. Each atom usually wants 8 outer electrons (or 2 for hydrogen).

Methane is CH4: carbon shares with 4 hydrogens. Ammonia is NH3: nitrogen shares with 3 hydrogens. Water is H2O. Carbon dioxide is CO2, with two double bonds.

Some covalent substances form huge networks instead of small molecules.

In diamond each carbon is bonded to 4 others, making it super hard. In graphite each carbon bonds to 3 others in sheets. Silicon dioxide (sand) is another giant covalent structure.

mcqs.q: Why does graphite conduct electricity but diamond does not?
options: Graphite has delocalised electrons between layers; diamond has all four outer electrons in localised covalent bonds.
Protons move from chlorine to sodium to balance the charges.
Graphite conducts because it can melt easily at room temperature.
Graphite conducts because it is a metal, while diamond is a non-metal.

mcqs.q: What happens to electrons when sodium reacts with chlorine?
options: Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
Sodium loses one electron to chlorine; the resulting Na+ and Cl- ions attract electrostatically.
Sodium and chlorine share an electron between them.
Protons move from chlorine to sodium to balance the charges.

mcqs.q: When water boils, what is broken?
options: Intermolecular forces (hydrogen bonds) between water molecules are broken — the O-H covalent bonds stay intact.
Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
The covalent bonds between hydrogen and oxygen atoms are broken when water boils.
Protons move from chlorine to sodium to balance the charges.
